title: Neither side denies the other’s act — assent, refuge, and consequent persuasion cohere
source_text: LXXXVI. Caeterum omnes illi quanquam in sua definitione mentionem non faciunt assensus quem fides salvifica praebet toti Verbo Dei, nihilominus fatentur talem assensum in fide includi, aut ad eam requiri, ut satis manifestum est ex iis quae ante fuerunt a nobis exposita. Nec etiam qui fidem describunt ab ea persuasione quam habet fidelis de Dei erga se gratia & benevolentia, negant in fide praecedere fiduciam illam qua quis Deo adhaeret, & ad eum confugit ut misericordiam ab eo consequatur. Sicut vicissim qui fidem definiunt a fiducia illa, qua quis in Deum recumbit, ut veniam & misericordiam ab eo obtineat, non negant in fide sequi alteram istam fiduciam, qua quis de Dei amore & benevolentia erga se persuasus est.
pass_a_gloss: But yet all those, although in their definition they make no mention of the assent which saving faith gives to the whole Word of God, nevertheless confess that such assent is included in faith, or required for it, as is sufficiently plain from those things which were previously set forth by us. Nor do those who describe faith from that persuasion which the believer has of God's grace and goodwill toward himself deny that there precedes in faith that trust by which one adheres to God and flees to him that he may obtain mercy from him. Just as in turn those who define faith from that trust by which one reclines upon God that he may obtain pardon and mercy from him do not deny that there follows in faith that other trust by which one is persuaded of God's love and goodwill toward himself.
pass_b_english: Those who omit whole-Word assent in the definition still confess it is included or required.
Grace-persuasion definers do not deny prior refuge-fiducia fleeing to God for mercy.
Refuge-fiducia definers do not deny consequent persuasion of God’s love and goodwill.
The acts cohere; definitions spotlight different moments.
